subproblems.title: Evaluation bound |T(ω)| ≤ r·M_W(T) when tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω| ≤ r (fact (E1))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, W ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) and r ∈ ℝ. Write |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α and M_W(T) := T.massOn W ∈ [0, ∞]. By Simon 6.2.5, M_W(T) is the supremum of ofReal T(φ) over φ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport φ ⊆ W and |φ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. If M_W(T) ≠ ∞, tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ r for every x ∈ ℝ^P, then |T(ω)| ≤ r·(M_W(T)).toReal.

Hence |t•α| = √(t²S) = |t|·√S = |t|·|α|. Also |α| ≥ 0, being a square root, and |−α| = |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
2. (r ≥ 0.) By hypothesis 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ r.
3. Put M := T.massOn W and m := M.toReal ≥ 0. Since M ≠ ∞, for every real a, ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ M implies a ≤ m (ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal).
4. (Admissible rescalings.) Fix ε > 0 and let s := r + ε > 0. Let ω' := s⁻¹ • ω, an element of TestFormOn U n (a submodule) whose underlying form is x ↦ s⁻¹•ω(x). Then tsupport ω' ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, since the tsupport of a scalar multiple is contained in the tsupport. By step 1, |ω'(x)| = s⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ r/s ≤ 1 for all x. Hence ω' ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W. Likewise −ω' ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, since it has the same tsupport and |−ω'(x)| = |ω'(x)|.

subproblems.title: Covectors with the coefficient norm form a Euclidean space
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ there are d ∈ ℕ and a continuous linear equivalence c from the space of n-covectors on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) n, with its operator-norm topology) onto ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) such that covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c(α)‖ for every n-covector α. Here covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_I)²)^{1/2}, with e_I = (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) for the standard basis e of ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ (d : ℕ) (c : Covector (Euclid P) n ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖

Reused comparator-accepted declaration (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.mass_representation-a1.covector_euclidean_equiv-a1, identical frozen type). Its accepted proof follows, with step 4 written out instead of citing that node's sibling.
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 1.15 and Remark 2.6 (the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors). The coefficient map is an isometry from |·| onto a Euclidean space; injectivity is proved by the sorting argument of step 4.
1. Notation. Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n; J := Fin n → Fin P, a finite type; for I ∈ J, e_I := (fun i => EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (I i)); F := EuclideanSpace ℝ J, a finite-dimensional real inner product space.
2. Coefficient map. Define A : Λ →ₗ[ℝ] F by A α := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun I => if StrictMono I then α e_I else 0). For each fixed I, α ↦ α e_I is additive and commutes with real scalars (it is evaluation of a continuous alternating map at a fixed tuple), so A is ℝ-linear.
3. Norm identity. By EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, ‖A α‖ = √(Σ_I ‖(A α) I‖²) = √(Σ_I (if StrictMono I then (α e_I)² else 0)). This uses ‖t‖² = t² for real t and (if p then a else 0)² = if p then a² else 0. The right-hand side is covectorEuclideanNorm α by definition.
4. Injectivity. Let A α = 0, i.e. α(e_I) = 0 for every strictly increasing I ∈ J. Let J' ∈ J be arbitrary. If J' is not injective, e_{J'} has two equal entries and α(e_{J'}) = 0 because α is alternating. If J' is injective, let I be the strictly increasing enumeration of its range and σ the permutation of Fin n with J' = I ∘ σ; since α is alternating, α(e_{J'}) = sign(σ)·α(e_I) = 0. For arbitrary v : Fin n → ℝ^P write v_i = Σ_k v_i^k e_k; multilinearity gives α(v) = Σ_{J'∈J} (Π_i v_i^{J'(i)})·α(e_{J'}) = 0. Hence α = 0 (ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext), and A is injective.
5. Isometric identification of the range. Let S := LinearMap.range A, a subspace of F; with the induced inner product it is a finite-dimensional real inner product space. Let d := finrank ℝ S and b := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ S, an orthonormal basis indexed by Fin d; b.repr : S ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) is a linear isometric equivalence. Let e₀ := LinearEquiv.ofInjective A (using step 4), so e₀ : Λ ≃ₗ[ℝ] S and (e₀ α : F) = A α. Let c₀ := e₀.trans b.repr.toLinearEquiv. Then ‖c₀ α‖ = ‖b.repr (e₀ α)‖ = ‖e₀ α‖ = ‖A α‖ = covectorEuclideanNorm α, since the norm of an element of a subspace is its ambient norm.
6. Continuity. Λ is finite-dimensional, being linearly equivalent to EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) via c₀ (LinearEquiv.finiteDimensional applied to c₀.symm). A linear equivalence between finite-dimensional real normed spaces is a homeomorphism, so c := c₀.toContinuousLinearEquiv : Λ ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) is a continuous linear equivalence. It satisfies ‖c α‖ = ‖c₀ α‖ = covectorEuclideanNorm α for all α.
7. Conclusion. d and c satisfy the claim. Consequently |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm is a norm on Λ: |α + β| ≤ |α| + |β|, |tα| = |t||α|, |α| = 0 iff α = 0, and |·| is continuous.
proof_key_steps: The coefficient map A, sending α to α(e_I) on strictly increasing I and to 0 elsewhere, into EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P) satisfies ‖Aα‖ = covectorEuclideanNorm α.
A is injective: an alternating form vanishing on all increasing basis tuples vanishes on all basis tuples (sorting with a sign), hence everywhere by multilinearity.
range A ≅ ℝ^d isometrically via an orthonormal basis; compose with LinearEquiv.ofInjective.
Finite-dimensionality upgrades the linear equivalence to a continuous linear equivalence.

subproblems.title: Basic calculus of integer multiplicity representations: locality of approximate tangent spaces, restriction, differences, orientation bound
subproblems.statement: (a) Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel sets with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) if and only if M' does. (b) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U (contract structure) and E is Borel, then (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and it represents some current in 𝒟_n(U). (c) If U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), then so is A − B. (d) For every IMRep R in any U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier, |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α (|·| the Euclidean coefficient norm).

Reused comparator-accepted declaration (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.im_calculus-a1, identical frozen type); its accepted proof follows (remarks about other DAG nodes omitted).
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the density argument in the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” (chapter-03.txt lines 107–160); Ch. 6, Remarks 3.2(1) and 2.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 287–293, 755–768), stated in the book without proof; and Ch. 6, Remark 2.6 for the orientation bound. Hⁿ := μHE[n] throughout. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). The statement has four parts: (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces, (b) restriction of a representation to a Borel set, (c) differences of integer multiplicity currents, (d) the orientation bound |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|; U is open in (a)–(c).

Preliminaries.
(P0) Normalization: SimonGMT's density theorems are stated for simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n, which equals μHE[n] for natural n (SimonGMT Chapter02 simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, with simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure); hence null sets, finiteness and densities transfer verbatim, and Hⁿ is Borel regular (every set has a Borel hull of the same measure).
(P1) Scaling: for every set A, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(A) (Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_smul₀ and invariance of Hausdorff measure under isometries). Hence for Borel A and bounded Borel f, ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A f(η_{x,r}(y)) dHⁿ(y).
(P2) Density zero (SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_3_6, for the Borel regular outer measure Hⁿ, cf. simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff): if D is Borel with Hⁿ(D) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ D, lim_{r↓0} Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) = 0.
(P3) Cauchy–Binet. For n×P matrices A, B, det(ABᵀ) = Σ_I det(A_I) det(B_I), the sum over increasing I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) in {1, …, P}, A_I the n×n submatrix of columns I. Proof: the j-th column of ABᵀ is Σ_k B_{jk}A_{·k}, so by multilinearity det(ABᵀ) = Σ_{k_1,…,k_n} B_{1k_1}⋯B_{nk_n} det(A_{·k_1}, …, A_{·k_n}); terms with a repeated index vanish, and grouping the remaining tuples by their underlying increasing tuple I (k = I ∘ σ for a permutation σ) gives Σ_I det(A_I) Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j B_{j, I_{σ(j)}} = Σ_I det(A_I)det(B_I). (For n > P both sides are 0 — no increasing I, and rank ABᵀ < n.)
(P4) Orientation bound. If τ_1, …, τ_n are orthonormal in ℝ^P and ⟨α, ζ⟩ = ±α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors α, then |⟨α, ζ⟩| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm). Proof: with A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I); by Cauchy–Schwarz and (P3), |α(τ)| ≤ |α|(Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2} = |α| det(AAᵀ)^{1/2} = |α|, since AAᵀ = (⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) is the identity. For n = 0, |α(∅)| = |α|.
(P5) Two unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace Q differ by a sign: if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of Q, τ'_i = Σ_j O_{ij}τ_j with O orthogonal, and α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating α. Hence IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' Q imply ζ' = ζ or ζ' = −ζ, and IsUnitOrientationOf (−ζ) Q holds whenever IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q.
(P6) If R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in an open U, then Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (θ ≥ 1 on M).

(d) Orientation bound. By the orientation field of an IMRep, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q, i.e. an orthonormal τ with ⟨α, R.orient x⟩ = ±α(τ) for all α; by (P4), |R.orient x α| ≤ |α| for all α. (No openness of U is needed.)

(a) Locality. Let U be open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and D := M' ∖ M.
1. For R ∈ ℕ let U_R := {x ∈ U : |x| < R, infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/R} (U_R := {|x| < R} if U = ℝ^P). U_R is open, closure(U_R) is a compact subset of U, and U_R ↑ U. D_R := D ∩ U_R is Borel with Hⁿ(D_R) ≤ Hⁿ(M' ∩ closure(U_R)) < ∞. By (P2) there is an Hⁿ-null set Z_R such that every x ∉ D_R ∪ Z_R satisfies Hⁿ(D_R ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ) as r ↓ 0. Let Z := ⋃_R Z_R, and let Z' ⊇ Z be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0). Let x ∈ M ∖ Z'; choose R with x ∈ U_R and r₀ > 0 with B̄_{r₀}(x) ⊆ U_R. Then x ∉ D_R (as x ∈ M) and D ∩ B̄_r(x) = D_R ∩ B̄_r(x) for r < r₀, so Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ).
2. Fix such x, a subspace Q and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_ρ(0). For r < r₀/ρ the sets η_{x,r}(M), η_{x,r}(M') meet B_ρ(0) in sets of finite Hⁿ-measure, so the integrals below are genuine Bochner integrals. Since η_{x,r} is injective, η_{x,r}(M') is the disjoint union of η_{x,r}(M) and η_{x,r}(D), and by (P1)
 |∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ| = |∫_{η_{x,r}(D)} f dHⁿ| ≤ |f|_∞ r^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{rρ}(x)) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
Hence for every f the two families of integrals have the same limit as r → 0⁺ or both have none; the condition finrank Q = n is common to both predicates. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q for every x ∈ M ∖ Z' and every Q; the exceptional set M ∩ Z' is null for Hⁿ⌞M. ∎

(b) Restriction. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in the open set U and E a Borel set. Define R' with carrier M ∩ E and the same mult θ and orient ξ.
1. Structure fields: M ∩ E is Borel and contained in U; countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono); θ is measurable and θ > 0 on M ∩ E; ∫_{M∩E∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M.
2. Orientation: by (P6) and (a) applied to M ∩ E ⊆ M ⊆ U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ E and all Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ E) x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. With the orientation field of R (Hⁿ-a.e. on M) this gives the orientation field of R'.
3. The current: A(ω) := ∫_{M∩E} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). By (d), |θ⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ |ω|_∞ θ 1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M, and tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, so the integrand is integrable; A is linear. If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges: supports in a fixed compact K ⊆ U and uniform convergence of all derivatives, in particular |ω_j|_∞ → 0 since all norms on the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors are equivalent), then |A(ω_j)| ≤ |ω_j|_∞ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ → 0. So A is a GeometricCurrentOn U n and R' represents A (IMRep.Represents, IMRep.action). ∎

(c) Differences. Let A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, be represented by R_A = (M_A, θ_A, ξ_A) and R_B = (M_B, θ_B, ξ_B).
1. (Borel versions and good points.) Choose Borel ξ̃_A, ξ̃_B equal to ξ_A, ξ_B Hⁿ-a.e. on M_A, resp. M_B (a.e. strong measurability; set them 0 off the carriers). Let G be the set of x ∈ M_A ∪ M_B such that: if x ∈ M_A, then ξ̃_A(x) = ξ_A(x) and there is Q_A(x) with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_A x Q_A(x) and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_A x) Q_A(x); the analogous condition for B if x ∈ M_B; and, for each pair (N, N') among (M_A ∩ M_B, M_A), (M_A ∩ M_B, M_B) with x ∈ N, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N' x Q for every Q. By the orientation fields of R_A, R_B, by (P6) and by (a), (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G is Hⁿ-null; let N₀ ⊇ (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0).
2. (Overlap.) Let x ∈ (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀. The approximate tangent space of M_A ∩ M_B at x exists and equals Q_A(x) and also Q_B(x) (the equivalences defining G and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces, SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique); so Q_A(x) = Q_B(x) and by (P5) ξ̃_B(x) = ε(x)ξ̃_A(x) with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1}. Put ε(x) := 1 if ξ̃_B(x) = ξ̃_A(x) and ε(x) := −1 otherwise (a Borel function).
3. (Data.) Put O := (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀, k := θ_A − εθ_B ∈ ℤ on O, and
 M := ((M_A ∖ M_B) ∪ (M_B ∖ M_A) ∪ {x ∈ O : k(x) ≠ 0}) ∖ N₀,
 θ := θ_A on M_A ∖ M_B, θ_B on M_B ∖ M_A, |k| on O, 0 elsewhere (Borel, ℕ-valued),
 ζ := ξ̃_A on M_A ∖ M_B, −ξ̃_B on M_B ∖ M_A, sign(k)ξ̃_A on O, 0 elsewhere (Borel).
For every x ∉ N₀: θ(x)1_M(x)ζ(x) = θ_A(x)1_{M_A}(x)ξ̃_A(x) − θ_B(x)1_{M_B}(x)ξ̃_B(x) (on O with k = 0 both sides vanish; on O with k ≠ 0, θ_Aξ̃_A − θ_Bεξ̃_A = kξ̃_A = |k| sign(k)ξ̃_A; the other cases are immediate).
4. (Representation.) For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), integrating ⟨ω, ·⟩ against both sides of step 3 (N₀ is null; all integrands are integrable by (d), since θ1_M ≤ θ_A1_{M_A} + θ_B1_{M_B}):
 ∫_M θ⟨ω, ζ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{M_A} θ_A⟨ω, ξ_A⟩ dHⁿ − ∫_{M_B} θ_B⟨ω, ξ_B⟩ dHⁿ = A(ω) − B(ω) = (A − B)(ω).
5. (Structure fields.) M is Borel, M ⊆ M_A ∪ M_B ⊆ U, and M is countably n-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_iUnion, CountablyRectifiable.mono). θ is Borel and ℕ-valued with θ ≥ 1 on M (|k| ≥ 1 where k ≠ 0), and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M_A∩K} θ_A dHⁿ + ∫_{M_B∩K} θ_B dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U. ζ is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable.
6. (Orientation.) For compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(M_A ∩ K) + Hⁿ(M_B ∩ K) < ∞ by (P6) applied to R_A, R_B. Apply (a) to the pairs (M ∩ M_A ⊆ M_A), (M ∩ M_A ⊆ M), (M ∩ M_B ⊆ M_B), (M ∩ M_B ⊆ M) (all Borel, contained in U, with locally finite Hⁿ-measure): for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ M_A the approximate tangent spaces of M and of M_A at x coincide (both equal that of M ∩ M_A), and similarly for M_B. Let x be such a point, x ∉ N₀. If x ∈ M_A, then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_A(x) and ζ(x) = ±ξ_A(x) (cases M_A ∖ M_B and O, using ξ̃_A(x) = ξ_A(x)), a unit orientation of Q_A(x) by (P5). If x ∈ M_B ∖ M_A, ζ(x) = −ξ_B(x) is a unit orientation of Q_B(x), the approximate tangent space of M at x. Hence the orientation field holds Hⁿ-a.e. on M.
So (M, θ, ζ) is an IMRep in U representing A − B, and A − B is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: (d): Cauchy–Binet gives Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ) = 1 for orthonormal τ, so |α(τ)| ≤ |α|.
(a): the density of Hⁿ⌞(M′∖M) vanishes at Hⁿ-a.e. point of M (SimonGMT simon_theorem_3_6 on an exhaustion of U), so the blow-up integrals of M and M′ have the same limits.
(b): all IMRep fields restrict; the orientation field transfers by (a); continuity of the restricted current from local integrability and (d).
(c): on the overlap the approximate tangent spaces agree a.e., so the orientations differ by a sign; combine multiplicities θ_A ∓ θ_B, drop cancellation points, and verify the IMRep fields with (a).

subproblems.title: Measure calculus of integer multiplicity representations and of their restrictions to Borel sets
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation in U (contract IMRep U n) with weight μ_R := θ Hⁿ⌞M (contract R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ, Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then (a) μ_R is absolutely continuous with respect to Hⁿ⌞M; (b) ξ is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable; (c) for every Borel set E and every IMRep R′ in U with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ: μ_{R′} = μ_R⌞E, and for every n-form ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ (no regularity assumed) the action R′(ω) = ∫_{M∩E} θ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ (contract IMRep.action) equals ∫_E ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dμ_R(x) (Bochner integrals).

Let ρ, s ∈ ℝ with 0 < ρ < s and B_s := ball(0, s) ⊆ U, and assume: (i) ∂S(β) = 0 for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(U) with tsupport β ⊆ B_s; (ii) A(ω) = ∫_{ball(0,ρ)} ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) (Bochner integral) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); (iii) M_{B_s}(∂A) < ∞ (SimonGMT massOn, Euclidean coefficient norm). Then there are Ŝ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) and an IMRep R′ in ℝ^P such that R′ represents Ŝ (so Ŝ is integer multiplicity), R′.measure = μ⌞ball(0, ρ), Ŝ(ω) = currentEval(S, ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(0, ρ), ∂Ŝ(β) = 0 for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport β ⊆ ball(0, ρ), and M_{ℝ^P}(∂Ŝ) ≤ M_{B_s}(∂A).

Siblings: im_calculus (IMC), part (b); imrep_restriction (RS), part (c); eval_mass_bound (E1).
Notation: n := m + 1; Hⁿ := μHE[n]; M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, μ := R.measure; B_r := ball(0, r); ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ := ξ(x)(α); |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; 𝒟^k(V) := TestFormOn V k (a form α belongs to 𝒟^k(V) iff it is smooth, compactly supported and tsupport α ⊆ V).

0. Preliminary facts.
 (F1) closedBall(0, ρ) ⊆ B_s ⊆ U since ρ < s; so B_ρ ⊆ U, and closedBall(0, ρ) is a compact subset of U.
 (F2) |tα| = |t|·|α| for t ∈ ℝ and every covector α: (tα)(e_I) = t·α(e_I), so Σ_I [I strictly increasing](tα)(e_I)² = t²·Σ_I [I strictly increasing]α(e_I)², and √(t²X) = |t|√X for X ≥ 0.
 (F3) If x ∉ tsupport α then α(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), hence ⟨α(x), ξ(x)⟩ = 0 by linearity of ξ(x).

1. (Restriction in U.) Apply (IMC)(b) to R and the Borel set E := B_ρ (U is open): there is an IMRep R₁ in U with carrier M ∩ B_ρ, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ (the current it represents is not needed). By (RS)(c) applied to R, E = B_ρ and R′ := R₁: R₁.measure = μ⌞B_ρ, and R₁.action(α) = ∫_{B_ρ} ⟨α, ξ⟩ dμ for every n-form α (no regularity required).

2. (The same data as a representation in ℝ^P.) Let R₂ be the IMRep in ℝ^P with carrier M ∩ B_ρ, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. Its fields measurableSet_carrier, rectifiable, measurable_mult, mult_pos, aestronglyMeasurable_orient and orients only involve carrier, multiplicity, orientation and Hⁿ, so they are those of R₁; carrier ⊆ ℝ^P is trivial. Local integrability: for every compact K, (M ∩ B_ρ) ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ closedBall(0, ρ), so ∫_{(M∩B_ρ)∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩closedBall(0,ρ)} θ dHⁿ < ∞, by monotonicity of the lower integral in the domain (lintegral_mono_set) and R.locallyIntegrable_mult for the compact set closedBall(0, ρ) ⊆ U (F1).

3. (The current Ŝ.) Apply (IMC)(b) to R₂ (domain ℝ^P, open) and E := ℝ^P: there are Ŝ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and an IMRep R′ in ℝ^P representing Ŝ, with carrier (M ∩ B_ρ) ∩ ℝ^P = M ∩ B_ρ, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. IMRep.measure and IMRep.action depend only on carrier, multiplicity and orientation, so R′.measure = R₁.measure = μ⌞B_ρ (the second claim), and for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P):
 Ŝ(ω) = R′.action(ω) = R₁.action(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ} ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ.   (∗)

4. (Agreement.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_ρ. Then ω is smooth with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U (F1), so ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and currentEval(S, ω) = S(ω) (definition of currentEval, positive branch). As R represents S, S(ω) = R.action(ω); by (RS)(c) applied to R, E = ℝ^P and R′ := R (R.carrier = R.carrier ∩ ℝ^P), R.action(ω) = ∫_{ℝ^P} ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ. For x ∉ B_ρ we have x ∉ tsupport ω, so the integrand vanishes (F3), and ∫_{ℝ^P} ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ = ∫_{B_ρ} ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). By (∗) this is Ŝ(ω).

5. (No boundary inside B_ρ.) Let β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport β ⊆ B_ρ. Then ∂Ŝ(β) = Ŝ(dβ) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply; dβ = exteriorDerivative β is a test form, exteriorDerivative_isTestForm), and tsupport dβ ⊆ tsupport β ⊆ B_ρ (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). By step 4, Ŝ(dβ) = currentEval(S, dβ) = S(dβ), with dβ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Also β ∈ 𝒟^m(U) (tsupport β ⊆ B_ρ ⊆ U), and S(dβ) = ∂S(β) because the exterior derivative of β ∈ 𝒟^m(U) is the same form dβ (boundary_apply). Since tsupport β ⊆ B_ρ ⊆ B_s, hypothesis (i) gives ∂S(β) = 0. Hence ∂Ŝ(β) = 0.

6. (Cut-off.) Put s′ := (ρ + s)/2, so ρ < s′ < s, and let χ : ℝ^P → ℝ be the smooth bump function centred at 0 with inner radius ρ and outer radius s′ (Mathlib ContDiffBump): χ is C^∞, 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on closedBall(0, ρ), tsupport χ = closedBall(0, s′) ⊆ B_s, χ has compact support, and for every x ∈ B_ρ, χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of x (ContDiffBump.eventuallyEq_one_of_mem_ball). Let β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with |β(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, and γ(x) := χ(x)·β(x).
 (a) γ is smooth (product of smooth maps) with compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right), and tsupport γ ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ B_s ⊆ U (tsupport_smul_subset_left). Thus γ ∈ 𝒟^m(U) and tsupport γ ⊆ B_s.
 (b) |γ(x)| = χ(x)·|β(x)| ≤ 1 for every x, by (F2) and 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1.
 (c) For x ∈ B_ρ, γ = β on a neighbourhood of x, so dγ(x) = dβ(x): the exterior derivative at x depends only on the germ at x (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq).

7. (Boundary mass.) With β, γ as in step 6:
 ∂Ŝ(β) = Ŝ(dβ) = ∫_{B_ρ} ⟨dβ, ξ⟩ dμ   by (∗)
  = ∫_{B_ρ} ⟨dγ, ξ⟩ dμ   (the integrands agree on B_ρ by 6(c); setIntegral_congr_fun)
  = A(dγ)   (hypothesis (ii) for the test form dγ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U))
  = ∂A(γ)   (boundary_apply).
 By (E1) applied in U to the current ∂A ∈ 𝒟_m(U), the set W := B_s, the form γ and r := 1 — legitimate by (iii), 6(a) and 6(b) — |∂A(γ)| ≤ (M_{B_s}(∂A)).toReal. Hence ofReal(∂Ŝ(β)) ≤ ofReal((M_{B_s}(∂A)).toReal) = M_{B_s}(∂A), the last equality by (iii). The forms admissible for M_{ℝ^P}(∂Ŝ) are exactly such β (the support condition tsupport β ⊆ ℝ^P is vacuous), so taking the supremum (sSup_le) gives M_{ℝ^P}(∂Ŝ) ≤ M_{B_s}(∂A).

8. (Conclusion.) Ŝ and R′ satisfy all five claims: representation and weight (step 3), agreement (step 4), vanishing boundary inside B_ρ (step 5) and the boundary mass bound (step 7). ∎

Then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) such that T_{φ(i)} ⇀ C, i.e. T_{φ(i)}(ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (WeaklyConvergesOn).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 2.15 and the remark after Theorem 3.11 (chapter-06.txt lines 318–333 and 889–891): currents with locally bounded mass have a weakly convergent subsequence. Simon derives 2.15 from the Banach–Alaoglu theorem in the spaces M_n(W) (after representing the T_q by measures, 2.7); here, for U = ℝ^P and convergence on smooth test forms (2.13), the same conclusion is proved directly by a separability and diagonal argument, so no representation theorem is needed.
Siblings: eval_mass_bound (E1); covector_equiv (NE).
Notation: 𝒟ⁿ := TestFormOn ℝ^P n; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; B_R := ball(0, R); c_R := (sup_j M_{B_R}(T_j)).toReal ∈ [0, ∞) for R ∈ ℝ (the supremum is finite by hypothesis). By (NE) fix d ∈ ℕ and a continuous linear equivalence c from n-covectors (Mathlib's operator-norm space) onto ℝ^d with |α| = ‖c(α)‖ for all α, and let κ := ‖c‖ ≥ 0 (operator norm), so |α| ≤ κ‖α‖.

1. (Uniform evaluation bound.) If R ∈ ℝ, ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ, tsupport ω ⊆ B_R and |ω(x)| ≤ r for all x, then |T_j(ω)| ≤ r·c_R for every j. Indeed M_{B_R}(T_j) ≤ sup_j M_{B_R}(T_j) < ∞, so (E1) (with U = ℝ^P, W = B_R) gives |T_j(ω)| ≤ r·(M_{B_R}(T_j)).toReal, and (M_{B_R}(T_j)).toReal ≤ c_R because toReal is monotone on finite values; r ≥ |ω(0)| ≥ 0.

2. (Test forms are bounded and supported in balls.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ. Its tsupport is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport ω ⊆ B_R for some R ∈ ℕ. The map x ↦ c(ω(x)) is continuous (ω is smooth, c continuous) with compact support (c(0) = 0), hence bounded: there is r with |ω(x)| = ‖c(ω(x))‖ ≤ r for all x. By step 1, |T_j(ω)| ≤ B_ω := r·c_R for every j.

3. (Separability.) Fix R ∈ ℕ, let 𝒯_R := {ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ : tsupport ω ⊆ B_R} and K_R := closedBall(0, R) (compact). Define ι : 𝒟ⁿ → C(K_R, ℝ^d) by ι(ω)(x) := c(ω(x)). The space C(K_R, ℝ^d) is second countable (Mathlib ContinuousMap.instSecondCountableTopology in Mathlib.Topology.ContinuousMap.SecondCountableSpace: K_R is second countable and locally compact, ℝ^d is second countable), and on the compact domain K_R its topology is that of the sup metric dist(f, g) = sup_{x∈K_R} ‖f(x) − g(x)‖ (ContinuousMap.instMetricSpace). So it is separable, its subset ι(𝒯_R) is separable (IsSeparable.of_separableSpace), and since the space is metrizable there is a countable t ⊆ ι(𝒯_R) with ι(𝒯_R) ⊆ closure t (IsSeparable.exists_countable_dense_subset). For each g ∈ t choose ω_g ∈ 𝒯_R with ι(ω_g) = g, and let D_R := {ω_g : g ∈ t}, a countable subset of 𝒯_R.
 Claim: for every ω ∈ 𝒯_R and ε > 0 there is ω′ ∈ D_R with |ω(x) − ω′(x)| < ε for all x ∈ ℝ^P. Since ι(ω) ∈ closure t, there is g ∈ t with dist(ι(ω), g) < ε (Metric.mem_closure_iff); put ω′ := ω_g. For x ∈ K_R: |ω(x) − ω′(x)| = ‖c(ω(x)) − c(ω′(x))‖ = dist(ι(ω)(x), ι(ω′)(x)) ≤ dist(ι(ω), ι(ω′)) < ε (ContinuousMap.dist_apply_le_dist). For x ∉ K_R: x lies outside tsupport ω and tsupport ω′ (both ⊆ B_R ⊆ K_R), so ω(x) = ω′(x) = 0 and |0| = 0 < ε.

4. (Diagonal subsequence.) D := ⋃_{R∈ℕ} D_R is countable. For j ∈ ℕ put X_j(ω) := T_j(ω) (ω ∈ D), an element of ℝ^D. By step 2 every X_j lies in Π_{ω∈D}[−B_ω, B_ω], which is compact by Tychonoff's theorem (isCompact_univ_pi), and ℝ^D (product topology) is first countable because D is countable. Hence (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq) there are a ∈ ℝ^D and a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with X_{φ(i)} → a, i.e. T_{φ(i)}(ω) → a(ω) for every ω ∈ D (tendsto_pi_nhds). (This is the Cantor diagonal argument.)

5. (Convergence on every test form.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ and ε > 0. Pick R ∈ ℕ with ω ∈ 𝒯_R (step 2) and put δ := ε/(4(c_R + 1)) > 0, so δ·c_R ≤ ε/4. By step 3 pick ω′ ∈ D_R ⊆ D with |ω(x) − ω′(x)| < δ for all x. The test form ω − ω′ has tsupport ⊆ tsupport ω ∪ tsupport ω′ ⊆ B_R (tsupport_sub), so by step 1 and linearity, |T_j(ω) − T_j(ω′)| = |T_j(ω − ω′)| ≤ δ·c_R ≤ ε/4 for every j. As (T_{φ(i)}(ω′))_i converges (step 4), it is Cauchy: there is N with |T_{φ(i)}(ω′) − T_{φ(i′)}(ω′)| < ε/2 for i, i′ ≥ N. By the triangle inequality |T_{φ(i)}(ω) − T_{φ(i′)}(ω)| < ε/4 + ε/2 + ε/4 = ε for i, i′ ≥ N. So (T_{φ(i)}(ω))_i is a Cauchy sequence of reals and converges (cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete); let ℓ(ω) be its limit.

6. (Linearity and bound.) By uniqueness of limits and the linearity of each T_{φ(i)}, ℓ(ω + η) = ℓ(ω) + ℓ(η) and ℓ(tω) = t·ℓ(ω); thus ℓ : 𝒟ⁿ → ℝ is ℝ-linear. Passing to the limit in step 1 (|T_{φ(i)}(ω)| → |ℓ(ω)|, le_of_tendsto'): if tsupport ω ⊆ B_R and |ω(x)| ≤ r for all x, then |ℓ(ω)| ≤ r·c_R.

7. (Continuity.) Let ω_q → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ (TestFormOnConverges): there is a compact K with tsupport ω_q ⊆ K for all q, and iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ω_q → 0 uniformly on K for every k. Choose R ∈ ℝ with K ⊆ B_R (K is bounded). For k = 0, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero) and iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 of the zero form vanishes, so sup_{x∈K} ‖ω_q(x)‖ → 0 (operator norm). Given ε > 0, let η := ε/(2(κ + 1)(c_R + 1)) > 0 and q₀ such that ‖ω_q(x)‖ < η for all x ∈ K and q ≥ q₀. Then for q ≥ q₀ and every x: if x ∈ K, |ω_q(x)| = ‖c(ω_q(x))‖ ≤ κ‖ω_q(x)‖ ≤ κη; if x ∉ K, then x ∉ tsupport ω_q, so ω_q(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). By step 6, |ℓ(ω_q)| ≤ κη·c_R ≤ η(κ + 1)(c_R + 1) = ε/2 < ε. Hence ℓ(ω_q) → 0.

8. (Conclusion.) By steps 6 and 7, ℓ together with this continuity property is a current C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn: a linear functional with the sequential continuity of step 7), and by step 5, T_{φ(i)}(ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ, i.e. WeaklyConvergesOn (i ↦ T_{φ(i)}) C, with φ strictly increasing. ∎

subproblems.title: Agreement on expanding balls transfers weak convergence and boundary vanishing to the limit
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, U_j ⊆ ℝ^P arbitrary sets and S_j ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U_j) (j ∈ ℕ), Ŝ_j, C ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) and ρ_j ∈ ℝ with ρ_j → ∞. Assume Ŝ_j ⇀ C (WeaklyConvergesOn), Ŝ_j(ω) = currentEval(S_j, ω) for every j and every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(0, ρ_j), and ∂Ŝ_j(β) = 0 for every j and every β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport β ⊆ ball(0, ρ_j). Then ∂C = 0 and S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^P in the sense of ConvergesWeakly (currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P)).

Source: parent proof, step 7 (agreement on expanding balls); cf. Simon Ch. 6, 2.13 (chapter-06.txt lines 308–313: weak convergence is convergence on each test form, and ∂ is continuous for it).
Notation: B_r := ball(0, r); 𝒟^k := TestFormOn ℝ^P k.

1. (Supports lie eventually inside the balls.) Every α ∈ 𝒟^k (any k) has compact, hence bounded, tsupport, so tsupport α ⊆ B_r for some r ∈ ℝ (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_ball). As ρ_j → ∞, ρ_j ≥ r for all large j, and then tsupport α ⊆ B_r ⊆ B_{ρ_j}.

2. (S_j ⇀ C.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}. By step 1 and the agreement hypothesis, currentEval(S_j, ω) = Ŝ_j(ω) for all large j. Since Ŝ_j(ω) → C(ω) (WeaklyConvergesOn), the sequence (currentEval(S_j, ω))_j, which eventually coincides with it, converges to C(ω) as well (Tendsto.congr'). This is ConvergesWeakly (j ↦ S_j) C.

3. (∂C = 0.) Let β ∈ 𝒟^m. By definition of the boundary, ∂Ŝ_j(β) = Ŝ_j(dβ) and ∂C(β) = C(dβ), with dβ ∈ 𝒟^{m+1} (exteriorDerivativeTestOn); hence ∂Ŝ_j(β) → ∂C(β) (WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary). By step 1 and the vanishing hypothesis, ∂Ŝ_j(β) = 0 for all large j, so the same sequence also converges to 0. Limits in ℝ are unique, so ∂C(β) = 0. As β is arbitrary, C.boundary = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). ∎
